name: datepicker
description: Asks someone for a date. A native date input, so every platform's own picker, keyboard handling, and screen reader support come for free. To show a month rather than ask for a day, use calendar.

use.when: a person picks one date by looking at a month, such as by its weekday or near today. For a date a person knows, use when-field.
use.not: showing a month, which is a calendar.

label.description: What the date is for: 'Due date', not 'Date'.

name.description: Form field name. Also the default id.

value.description: The date already chosen, as YYYY-MM-DD.

min.title: Earliest allowed
min.description: As YYYY-MM-DD. The browser refuses earlier dates.

hint.description: Help text under the label. Say a limit in words when there is one: From 1 September 2026.

error.description: Validation message. Sets aria-invalid and is linked with aria-describedby.

keyboard.does: moves focus to and from the field; within it, the browser's own keys move between and change its parts, and open its calendar, which differ from browser to browser

wcag.notes: A native date input rather than a built calendar widget, so the keyboard model, the picker, and the announcements are the platform's own and work in every assistive technology without our code. On a phone it cannot be typed into and voice control reaches it poorly, so a date a person knows is asked for with when-field, in words. Label always visible; min and max are not enforced by every browser, so the server checks again, and a limit that matters is said in the hint in words. The icon is at full strength, and the calendar follows a theme chosen outright.

machine.identify: The accessible name is the label text. The value is an ISO date, YYYY-MM-DD.
machine.operate: Set the input's value to an ISO date. No need to open the picker.

props.label: Deadline
props.name: deadline
props.error: Deadline must be in the future.
